name: Buyer-set protein product challenge lab
what: A credit-bearing, one-semester product-design course at one or two Vietnamese food-technology faculties, with a short technical foundations module before it. Student teams of three to five work on problems set, and partly paid for, by Vietnamese buyers: chay makers, plant-milk makers, ingredient distributors and fermenters. Problems are T1, T9 and T10 products and specifications, using local raw materials and food-grade side streams. Teams present at an annual showcase, for example a table at the existing FID contest.
why_vietnam: The study's skills gap is specialist: almost no Vietnamese work on sensory and structure of meat analogues, extrusion or protein-quality scoring (ch06). T1 and T10 need a buyer specification and functional trials before a plant (ch26). HUIT's FID contest already draws nearly 500 contestants and 144 projects from 58 institutions and runs a firm-judged table, but its 2025 winners included no plant-protein product. We found no credit-bearing alternative-protein course (L6 to confirm). Berkeley ran this format from Spring 2017 to Spring 2024 with about 32 students a semester and at least three startups; a Brazilian egg producer used it to localise a plant egg with Brazilian crops.
must_be_true: A host faculty with a pilot kitchen and basic analysis (proximate, texture); at least two firms that set problems and give samples and staff time; a lecturer with industry R&D experience; teaching load recognised by the university; access to an extruder or pilot line for T1 work (IUH or FIRI; links to T5 and P4).
kill_tests: No Vietnamese firm sets and co-funds a problem for the first cycle; fewer than 15 students enrol in each of the first two cycles; no firm runs its own trial of a team's prototype or specification within two cycles.
first_customers: Food-technology faculties (HUIT, IUH, HUST, Can Tho University, Nong Lam University) as hosts; problem-setting firms such as chay makers (An Nhien, Au Lac), plant-milk makers (Vinamilk, TH) and ingredient distributors
partners: VAFoST and the National Startup Support Center (FID co-organisers); FID organisers at HUIT; SCET global partnership route (Chulalongkorn and Sunway are regional partners; no Vietnamese partner); funders under RM-11
capital_note: Low. Berkeley's lab received USD 125,000 from the Open Philanthropy Project in 2019 to expand its programme (period not stated). Vietnamese cost not estimated.
